title: Relational databases from Codd model through System R, SQL and cost-based optimization
pressure: Large databases were hard to query because applications depended on physical record layouts and navigation paths; new questions required specialist programs.
preExistingWorldModel: Hierarchical/network databases worked and were optimized around known access paths. Codd proposed separating logical relations from physical storage, but performance was uncertain.
candidateRoutes: relational model plus high-level query language
observationsAndInstruments: Codd formalized relations and data independence in 1970.
IBM System R tested the model as an industrial prototype.
SQL exposed set-oriented queries above storage paths.
Cost-based optimization translated declarative queries into physical plans.
decisiveTests: answer useful workloads without exposing record navigation
optimizer-selected plans compete with expert hand-crafted paths
technicalOrScientificTransition: A declarative representation became practical only when hidden physical optimization, transactions and storage machinery could honor it at acceptable cost; abstraction and implementation were co-produced.
rivalsAndFailures: Conceptual simplicity could require implementation sophistication underneath.
High-level queries did not remove physical layout, indexes or cost estimation.
Early performance skepticism could be rational before prototype closure.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: A declarative representation became practical only when hidden physical optimization, transactions and storage machinery could honor it at acceptable cost; abstraction and implementation were co-produced.
sourceNativeSummary: A declarative representation became practical only when hidden physical optimization, transactions and storage machinery could honor it at acceptable cost; abstraction and implementation were co-produced.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
Which later narrative compresses materially distributed work?
